title: A label read back into text comes back at the size its neighbours are, not its own
goal: Reading the labels of a screenshot back into real text now settles the typeface and the weight for the whole page, so six identical row labels come back as one. The point size is still decided label by label: those same six come back 27.6, 27.1, 28.5, 28.0, 28.5 and 28.4 points when every one of them is 13 points on screen, so picking them all shows Size reading Mixed. Anybody who then sets a size is tidying up after the app. Settle the size the way the weight is settled, for labels of one kind, without dragging a heading down to its rows.
notes: Found on 2026-09-17 finishing a-label-read-back-into-text-comes-back-in-the-we, which settled the WEIGHT and is done; see queue/audits/2026-09-17-label-weight.json and the screenshot beside it, where the Text section reads Font SF Pro, Weight Regular, Size Mixed for six labels picked together. The machinery to copy is already there and is pure: TextReading.WeightBallot groups the runs of a page into cohorts of one size and one ink colour (TextReading.weightCohorts) and TextReading.pageWeights settles each cohort. The size question is not identical though, and that is the interesting part: the weight is one of four values so a vote works, while the size is continuous, so the answer is probably the cohort s median fit rounded to something a person would type, and it has to stay inside the tolerance theRetypedWordsAreTheSizeTheOldOnesWere holds (3 px on the ink box). Careful with the two scales: the size a cohort is grouped BY is at captureScale, and the size a layer is SET at is at layerScale, and TextReader.settle is where the second one is worked out. Note the cohort sizes above are at 2x (13 points of type in a 2x capture opened whole is a 27ish point layer).
acceptance: Labels that are the same size in the picture come back at the same size, decided across the page rather than per label
A heading over its rows, and a section label over the rows under it, still come back bigger where they are bigger: the rule settles wobble, it does not flatten a page to one size
The retyped words still cover the space the picture s ink covered, within the tolerance theRetypedWordsAreTheSizeTheOldOnesWere already holds the reader to
Try it: Next release, open the settings pane fixture, separate it, press Read the Words, pick all six row labels and the Size menu reads one number instead of Mixed
Covered by the fixture tests that read the real 2x settings pane and effects panel captures, with the size asserted the way the weight is
A walk covers it, and it is named on the task with queue.mjs walks

log.note: Adversarial review before building: the mock is not the question here, the RULE is. Three things could have gone wrong and were checked on real captures before a line landed. (1) A page-wide size would flatten a heading onto its rows: rejected, the cohorts are the weight vote's, which already keep General and the section labels apart. (2) Rounding to a whole point, which the task suggested: MEASURED and rejected, holding the settings pane's six rows to 28 rather than 28.38 drops Copy to clipboard to 0.502 agreement, under landedBar, so a label that was meant to come back tidy would not come back at all, and it lands 3px short of the ink. The Size menu truncates to whole points anyway, so all six read 28 px either way. (3) Converting the size the face was identified at into the size the layer is set at by scale alone: rejected, measured they differ 6 to 10 per cent per run because an antialiased edge does not scale, so the size is settled in the size the layer is SET at.

Shipped. TextReading.pageSize/pageSizes in PhotonzCore settle each weight cohort on the MIDDLE of the sizes its runs fit at; TextReader.holdEachToItsCohortsSize re-sets each run at it and keeps the run's own size when the settled one cannot account for its ink (agreement under landedBar), so settling a size never costs a reading, exactly as settling a weight never does. Settings pane: rows 1-7 all 28.38 (were 27.6 to 28.5). Effects panel: rows 22.22, sections 23.03. Every retyped word still covers its ink within 2px of 3 allowed.

Found while verifying, and fixed here because it made the feature look broken in its own screenshot: a text box exactly as wide as its words was being cut with an ellipsis on the canvas at some zooms. A box is measured in document points and drawn through a zoom, the canvas states the frame in output pixels and the rasterizer divides it back, and w*zoom/zoom is not always w in binary floating point. One ulp cost three characters: 'Show in menu bar' drew as 'Show in menu b…' at 151%. Reproduced at the arithmetic (154 of 2000 zoom steps in a thousandth either side of the walk's zoom put that width under) and in the app (screenshot before and after, old build reproduced with the change stashed). TextRasterizer.truncationSlack = 0.01pt, covered by two tests in OneLineTextRenderTests. Shared code, so Current gets the fix too, which is right: it is a defect, not a Next behaviour.

Labels of one kind come back at one size. TextReading.pageSize/pageSizes (PhotonzCore, pure) settle each weight cohort on the middle of the sizes its runs fit at; TextReader.holdEachToItsCohortsSize re-sets each run at it and keeps the run's own size where the settled one cannot account for its ink. Settings pane rows all 28.38 (were 27.6-28.5), Effects panel rows 22.22 and sections 23.03, every retyped word within 2px of its ink. Verified: full suite 8197 green, 9 new core tests, 4 new settings-pane fixture tests and 4 new effects-panel ones, label-size-walk (60 steps, 6 real window captures) green and failing on the old build at step 23 with Mixed. Also fixed a hairsbreadth truncation in TextRasterizer that made 'Show in menu bar' draw as 'Show in menu b…' on the canvas. Audit queue/audits/2026-09-17-label-size.json. Commit 12364a49.
